title: Future of marketing panel: vision, intuition over data, and press as a lasting channel
summary: Growth Tribe panel with Pieter Levels, Marc Köhlbrugge and others on shipping early, engineered marketing and data. The transcript has no speaker labels, so only the clearest Levels-style statements are kept: visualizing the future as the source of products, trusting intuition over A/B testing, and press as a sustained traffic source. Attribution is low confidence.

principles.text: Products start from a vividly visualized future vision that you already carry inside you, then get built in small steps.
principles.quote: you don't need search for vision it's already in you you just have to you know dig into yourself

principles.text: Rely on intuition and feel for your product more than analytics and endless A/B testing.
principles.quote: I don't really trust it I think you should go for your intuition like have a feeling about your product and how you would use it

principles.text: Over-optimizing conversion can win sales but leave customers who feel tricked; aim for happy customers, not maximal extraction.
principles.quote: you don't need to be you know optimize everything - it's not all about sales dude it's about having fun

principles.text: Press works as a sustained channel, but only if a good product backs it; old articles keep sending traffic.
principles.quote: you need to have a product that actually backs it because people want to read something and then they go to your product and if it sucks they're you know they're not going to care

principles.text: Paid retargeting was not worth it for him; he stays distrustful of it after testing.
principles.quote: I tried retargeting and I spent like two thousand dollars on Facebook
